clue.text: Challenge story about crook, Australian native having escaped

indicators.note: the story goes about, round, what remains of crook

parts.note: a story is a tale

indicators.note: the animal having escaped means its letters leave the word crook

parts.note: taken as written before the animal leaves it
ROO, short for kangaroo, the animal native to Australia

explanation.surface: A challenge to a tale about a criminal whose kangaroo has run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal, but it is just letters; 'having escaped' takes the kangaroo out, and 'about' wraps the story round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem or opponent is to take it on directly, a synonym.

clue.text: South winds accompanied by a couple of monkeys in total?

definitions.text: a couple of monkeys in total?

indicators.note: winds, as a verb, means twists, so the letters of south are turned about

parts.note: and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: Southerly winds bring along a pair of monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a monkey is five hundred pounds, so two of them make a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Two monkeys, British slang for 500 pounds each, add up to one thousand.

clue.text: Cold twisted metal is for plant

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: twisted means bent into a different form, so the letters of metal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cold twisted metal is used in place of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges only metal; 'is' stays as written and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant with large showy flowers.

clue.text: Member worried papal emissary

parts.note: a limb is a member, here a leg
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A member of the church is anxious about a papal envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a representative sent by the Pope with his authority.

clue.text: Curry that's sensational!

definitions.meaning: a fiery curry is very spicy fare
something sensational is thrilling or highly attractive

explanation.surface: Someone praises a curry as a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both very spicy food and anything exciting, two idiomatic senses.

clue.text: Bald tramp on English instrument

indicators.note: bald means without a top, so the head letter of the tramp goes

parts.note: a hobo is a homeless wanderer

explanation.surface: A bald vagrant plays an English instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Suspiciously, she and I welcoming dubious charmer

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the shuffled letters surround the doubtful word
suspiciously says the letters are dodgy and must be rearranged

parts.note: a moot point is open to doubt

explanation.surface: She and I suspiciously welcome a shady charmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspiciously' rearranges she and I, and 'welcoming' places the doubtful word inside that jumble after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a suave, ingratiating man, a charmer.

clue.text: Warm out?

definitions.meaning: warm is not cold, taking cool as the opposite of hot

explanation.definitionFit: Literally not cold, so warm, and slang for unfashionable or square, as out-of-date things are.

clue.text: Good, more elegant dresses, one on hand

indicators.note: dresses means clothes, covers, so the finer word wraps round the letter

parts.note: finer means more refined or elegant

explanation.surface: A good and smarter outfit, one available.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger is one of the digits on a hand, the definition read literally.

clue.text: Nervous individual, loveless old magistrate

parts.note: an individual is one

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, which leaves

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice and Genoa

explanation.surface: A lonely, unloved former magistrate is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O (love, nil in tennis) from DOGE, leaving DGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being tense and jumpy.

clue.text: Imbecile bagging double century, a north African

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so the fool's letters enclose the hundreds

parts.note: an imbecile is a moron

indicators.note: double says the hundred letter appears twice in a row

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A fool scores two hundred runs and turns out to come from north Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'century' sounds like cricket runs here, but it is just the Roman numeral; 'bagging' means the fool's letters hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Morocco is a native of that north African kingdom, a demonym.

clue.text: Father figure in transport of goods

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
eight is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A priest appears as a figure in the haulage business.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo or the carriage of goods by road, rail or sea.

clue.text: Harlot taking one pole after — another?

parts.note: S is the south pole
the latter comes after
N, the other (north) pole

explanation.surface: A prostitute takes up with one pole dancer after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another pole: S and N are the two ends of the Earth or a magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a slovenly woman, and dated usage extends it to a prostitute.

clue.text: Pet rower

definitions.meaning: to pet is to caress gently with the hand
the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace for the crew

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a caressing touch of the hand and the pace-setting oarsman in a racing eight.

clue.text: Articulate rogue for a quickie?

indicators.note: articulate means say clearly, so the word is pronounced

parts.note: a rogue is a cheater, a dishonest person

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking rogue goes for a quick fling.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the fastest land animal, so a quick one in the playful sense.

clue.text: Arrest nefarious arsonist and larcenist initially

clue.text: Habit observed in close game

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A routine is noticed during a tight contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is a garment here, not a routine; 'observed in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a piece of clothing, as a nun's habit, and this is a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Battle of the campanologists?

parts.note: campanologists are bell-ringers, and bells go with this noise; the phrase also means a fierce fight

explanation.definitionFit: A fiercely contested fight is called this, and the phrase echoes the sound of bells being rung.

clue.text: Bordeaux served with first of dhansaks and Indian potato — 4 across!

parts.note: vin is French for wine, which Bordeaux is

indicators.note: picks the opening letter of the word dhansaks

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato

explanation.surface: A Bordeaux wine served with dhansaks and potato makes a hot Indian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A dhansak is a Parsi curry; 4 across is the curry clue answered elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiercely spicy curry, the very example of hot food.

clue.text: Animal about to trap girl unlike Goldilocks?

indicators.note: the beast goes about, round, the trap

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A beast is about to catch a girl who has no golden hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as about to happen; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldilocks is fair-haired, so a dark-haired girl is her opposite.

clue.text: Barge carrying less cargo?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed boat used to ferry goods to and from ships
having a smaller load, so weighing less

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cargo barge and is also the comparative of a word meaning not heavy.

clue.text: Phoney bar overhauled

indicators.note: overhauled taken as hauled over, so the bar is turned round end to end

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A fake bar has been refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoney is a fraud, someone who tells untruths, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Soul man supporting Paul Simon, Yazz and Cher for starters

indicators.note: in a down light the supporting word sits below, so it comes last
for starters picks the opening letters of the four singers' names

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A soul singer opens for Paul Simon, Yazz and Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the soul or mind, the inner self.

clue.text: Game of chance after first of bombs — under the table!

indicators.note: the game comes after the first letter
picks the opening letter of the word bombs

parts.note: lotto is a lottery or bingo-like game

explanation.surface: A game of chance follows a bombing, leaving everyone under the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk enough to slide under the table is very drunk, slang for which is this word.

clue.text: An air of pressure?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a melody and stress or tension.

clue.text: In herb, dill essentially is animal feed

indicators.note: the centre of dill goes in the herb

parts.note: sage is a herb

indicators.note: essentially means the essence or core of the word dill, its central letters

explanation.surface: Inside a herb, the dill is basically fodder for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented green fodder stored in a silo and fed to cattle.

clue.text: Old mammal mashing toads during the day

indicators.note: the jumbled toads come during, inside, the day

parts.note: MON is short for Monday

indicators.note: mashing means crushing into a new form, so the letters of toads are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone spends the day mashing toads, an old animal pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was a prehistoric elephant-like mammal, now extinct.

clue.text: Film clip from Stepmom is tedious

indicators.note: clip from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film clip from Stepmom is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a thin layer, and a light haze over glass is one.

clue.text: Prayer of interest to all

definitions.meaning: one who prays, here a member of the Roman church
universal, wide-ranging, as in broad tastes

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a member of the Roman church, and in lower case means universal or broad in scope.

clue.text: Hammer, hook, line and sinker confiscated by the police

indicators.note: the police take the whole lot into their keeping, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
the idiom means completely, the whole lot, all

explanation.surface: A hammer and all the fishing tackle are seized by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet is a wooden-headed hammer, used for croquet or chisels.

clue.text: Stretch toe, angle crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A stretching exercise for the toe has left it bent at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate something is to make it longer, to draw it out.

clue.text: Pay incorporated with 'ouse

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after US company names
the Cockney 'ouse drops its H, so home without its H gives the letters

explanation.surface: Wages come included with a house, said in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ouse' is house with the H dropped; the same dropping applied to home leaves OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is money received, the same as earnings or income.
